protocol.baseline_policy: Persistent repo Python kernel, same-model incremental summary of complete older messages in bounded chunks plus live kernel inventory. All summary calls/cost included. No resets.

reused_script_control.policy: Reuse both complete predeclared Python sessions; no score selection, rerun or rejudging. Baseline source, inputs and request policy match.

limitations: Two selected 19-turn prefixes, one repetition each; no benchmark-wide or isolated causal state-primitive claim.
Native source b008d435a produced valid runs; completion guard was added afterwards. Baseline controls reused in full with strict source/input/policy equality.
All requests fit the 32k input cap; no demonstrated feasibility win under a binding limit.
Same input inventory, not identical security isolation: native engine has broader host filesystem access than baseline mounts.
Automatic partial rubric remains unscored for unknown JSON layouts. Manual field aliases are post-run diagnostics, not altered official scores.
Manual error findings are targeted and do not classify every failed turn or establish every cascade cause.
Uniform frozen-rate estimates exclude judging and unknown-usage rejected API requests; not provider invoices.
Concurrent sessions and logged phases limit controlled latency and CPU interpretations.

decision.on_demand: experimental opt-in; cheaper than full in this pilot but less accurate and still more costly than DSGym
next_priorities: Reduce redundant inspections and model calls.
Use a typed Python action control to distinguish text-protocol/model failures from state-management effects.
Only test a memory-efficiency claim under a demonstrably binding input budget.
